target_customer: Restaurants and restaurant groups in Southeast Asia that want to sell directly instead of through delivery apps
problem: Delivery apps charge heavy commissions and keep customer data, so restaurants lose margin and the customer relationship.
business_model: B2B SaaS for direct ordering, with delivery rider booking and payments

founders.name: Jeroen Rutten
prior_employers: Google (6 years, product roles incl. Search and Measurement in APAC)

founders.name: Mathieu Sneep
founders.background_notes: About 10 years of sales and people management.

technical_complexity.rationale: Online ordering storefronts with payments and a rider booking integration were standard web engineering for a three person team.

defensibility.rationale: Restaurants could swap ordering tools easily, though integrations with POS and delivery partners added some friction.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Delivery platforms stayed commission based; Tablevibe partnered with DoorDash in 2022 for delivery fulfilment rather than competing head on.

market_need_then: Restaurants were complaining about delivery app commissions after the 2020 to 2021 delivery boom; Tablevibe's pitch claims savings of up to 80% against marketplace fees (company claim).

branding.domain_note: Uses tablevibe.co; co-founder Mathieu Sneep said in an interview they liked the startup feel of a .co.

identity.logo: Wordmark logo in site header, design not described by sources
identity.visual_style: Product screenshots and demo GIFs, restaurant brand logos as social proof
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and benefit driven: 0% commission, no setup fees.

brand_strength.rationale: Covered by TechCrunch and regional tech press and shows recognisable restaurant customers, but no evidence of community or word of mouth beyond that.

outcome_analysis: Tablevibe raised a 1.5M seed in November 2021 led by Global Founders Capital and signed delivery and payment partners including DoorDash, GCash and Deliverect, with large restaurant brands on its site. The YC directory lists it as Acquired, but no acquirer or date could be found and the company's own site and partner news show it still operating, so the real outcome is unclear.
notes: Directory status is Acquired but the outcome search found no deal, buyer or date; exit.type is set to unknown for that reason (one aggregator also says Acquired; a CB Insights Acquired flag belongs to a different company, TakeOut7). Total raised conflicts across aggregators (1.62M to 1.63M vs 130K); only the 1.5M seed is recorded. No competitor source dated near mid 2021 was found; Oddle appears on the company's own help page as a comparison, undated, so it is not listed. Seed article names the YC deal and angels without amounts.
